from.place: Step 2 statement: the finite coefficient, finite Tate line, and normalized tensor data used to form the signed twists

title: Finite Tate line data and signed comparison interface
statement: For a scheme $T$, a prime $\ell$, a finite commutative coefficient ring $A$ in the site universe, a natural-number level $n$, and a coefficient map $a:\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1}\to A$, use the canonical finite coefficient sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], its scalar map from the finite root coefficient ring, the finite Tate line obtained by scalar extension of the roots-of-unity module [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], and its normalized pure-tensor section. These are the canonical finite Tate coefficient, scalar, line, and tensor constructions recorded by the four declarations in the Lean record.
